context:
Goal: a small second fix after a passed fix check costs little, and fix checks never stand in for review rounds.
Problem (rule): your pick 418 b makes every fix after a passed fix check start a fresh chain of 3 more rounds; your note asked whether a capped chain could be allowed instead.
Based on (measured): review records on 575 PRs opened since 2026-11-02: 322 chains had a fix check; 294 (91%) had one, 28 (9%) had two, none recorded three. Read by script over issue comments at about 10:12 CST Nov 8.
Based on (measured): main refuses a second fix check, so longer chains went to fresh chains or void notes (59 PRs carry such a note, an upper bound by pattern count). One known case needed three: PR #1892.
Departs from: main, where a record takes one fix check and then a new round — up to N fix checks per chain, then a fresh chain.
Meanwhile: #1829 closes per 418 b, and the stack's standalone parts are rebuilt without chaining. In every option, a failed or wide fix check ends the chain, and after round 3 every link keeps the net-value test.

options.gain: Covers every chain recorded this week, and saves a fresh chain of 3 rounds on about 9% of chains.
options.how: A chain may hold two fix checks; a third small fix starts a fresh chain.
options.label: Cap at 2 fix checks per chain
options.lose: A third small fix still pays for a fresh chain.

options.how: A chain may hold three fix checks.
options.label: Cap at 3
options.lose: One more fix with no full review in each chain, for a shape seen once this week.

options.gain: Simplest: each fix check sits right after a review round.
options.how: One fix check per chain, then a fresh chain.
options.label: No chaining, as 418 b ruled
options.lose: About 28 chains a week pay a fresh chain of 3 rounds for a second small fix.
